generatedFrom: 8-Week Evidence-Based Puppy Training Curriculum (AVSAB / Dunbar Academy, cross-checked vs No Bad Dogs Kickstart)

idealTimes.label: Morning Active & Social Block
idealTimes.why: Freshest attention span of the day, right after morning potty + breakfast digestion, before Nap #1.

idealTimes.label: Midday Active Block
idealTimes.why: Post-lunch energy window before Nap #2; good for reinforcing morning lessons.

idealTimes.label: Afternoon Exposure & Walk
idealTimes.why: Only outdoor/exploration block long enough for controlled exposure work, still within the 15-min walk cap.

idealTimes.label: Stationed Settle & Chew
idealTimes.why: Naturally lower arousal before bedtime; ideal for calm, low-energy skills.

generalTips: Keep every session 5–10 minutes; stop before Simba loses interest, not after.
Train 2–3x/day using the blocks above, never right after a big meal or right before a nap.
Always end on a success — finish with an easy, known command for a final reward.
Use high-value treats (small, soft, smelly) for new skills; kibble is fine for review of mastered skills.

weeks.title: Foundations — Name, Hand Target, Sit, Crate Love, Handling

exercises.name: Name Recognition ("Watch Me")
exercises.goal: Simba looks at your face on cue.
exercises.steps: Say "Simba" once. The instant he glances at you, mark and reward. Repeat 10x per session.
exercises.rewardTiming: Immediately, every time.
exercises.mistake: Repeating the name multiple times before he responds — say it once.

exercises.name: Hand Target ("Touch")
exercises.goal: Nose touches your open palm on cue.
exercises.steps: Hold palm 2 inches from his nose. He'll sniff/touch it — mark + treat. Add the word "touch" once reliable. Increase distance gradually.
exercises.rewardTiming: Mark the instant nose contacts palm.
exercises.mistake: Moving your hand toward his nose instead of waiting for him to close the distance.

exercises.name: Sit
exercises.goal: Sit on cue without physical pressure.
exercises.steps: Lure with a treat from nose up and back over his head. Mark the instant hips touch ground. Add verbal "sit" once offered 80% without a lure.
exercises.rewardTiming: Mark exactly when hips touch floor.
exercises.mistake: Pushing down on his rear — unnecessary and risky for open growth plates.

exercises.name: Crate Love
exercises.goal: Crate stays a jackpot zone, not just a sleep box.
exercises.steps: Toss treats into the open crate at random times through the day, unconnected to training sessions.
exercises.rewardTiming: Random, throughout the day.
exercises.mistake: Only using the crate for confinement/timeouts.

exercises.name: Cooperative Handling
exercises.goal: Accepts paws, ears, mouth, tail touched calmly.
exercises.steps: Touch one paw for 1 second, mark + treat, release. Repeat on all paws, ears, tail; gently open mouth. Increase duration through the week.
exercises.rewardTiming: Mark right after each brief touch.
exercises.mistake: Restraining him if he struggles — back off and shorten duration instead.

exercises.name: Bite Inhibition
exercises.goal: Soft mouth; no escalation of play-biting.
exercises.steps: When teeth touch skin, freeze, give a calm "ah-ah," then redirect to a chew toy immediately.
exercises.rewardTiming: Praise once he engages the toy instead.
exercises.mistake: Yelping dramatically or yanking your hand away — can turn it into a chase game.

exercises.name: Down
exercises.goal: Lie down on cue from a sit.
exercises.steps: From sit, lower a treat straight down between front paws. Mark the instant belly/elbows touch. Add "down" once reliable.
exercises.rewardTiming: Mark at elbow contact with floor.
exercises.mistake: Pulling his front legs forward manually.

exercises.name: Come (Indoors Only)
exercises.goal: Reliable recall inside the house.
exercises.steps: Crouch, say "Simba, come!" happily, back away slightly. Mark on arrival, jackpot reward (3–4 treats) + praise.
exercises.rewardTiming: Jackpot immediately on arrival.
exercises.mistake: Calling him to come for something unpleasant (nail trims, ending play).

exercises.name: Place (Reward-Only Method)
exercises.goal: All four paws on a mat/bed, calmly, on cue.
exercises.steps: Toss a treat onto the mat. Mark the instant all 4 paws land on it, reward again while he's there. Release with "okay," toss a treat off. Add duration in small increments (2s, 5s, 10s).
exercises.rewardTiming: Mark on paw contact, then intermittent rewards while staying.
exercises.mistake: Using leash pressure or corrections if he steps off — instead, re-lure him back on and build duration more slowly.

exercises.name: Leash Introduction (No Pressure)
exercises.goal: Leash and harness become neutral, boring equipment.
exercises.steps: Clip the back-clip harness, let him drag the leash during supervised indoor play.
exercises.rewardTiming: N/A — passive habituation.
exercises.mistake: Any tugging or correction at this stage.

weeks.title: Stay, Leave It, Loose-Leash Indoors, Calm Greetings

exercises.name: Stay
exercises.goal: Holds sit/down position with duration and distance.
exercises.steps: Ask for sit, say "stay," wait 1s, mark + reward while still sitting, release with "okay." Add duration in 2–3s increments, then add one step of distance (reset duration to zero first).
exercises.rewardTiming: Mark while still in position, before release.
exercises.mistake: Increasing duration and distance at the same time — train one variable at a time.

exercises.name: Leave It
exercises.goal: Ignores a tempting item on cue.
exercises.steps: Show a treat in a closed fist. The instant he backs off or looks away, mark + reward from your OTHER hand.
exercises.rewardTiming: Reward from the opposite hand, never the fist he pestered.
exercises.mistake: Rewarding from the same fist he was pawing at.

exercises.name: Loose-Leash Walking (Indoors/Driveway)
exercises.goal: Stays near your leg without pulling.
exercises.steps: Hold a treat at your side, take one step, reward for staying near your leg. Add steps gradually. If he pulls, stop ("be a tree") and wait for slack.
exercises.rewardTiming: Reward while walking calmly at your side.
exercises.mistake: Any leash pops or corrections for pulling.

exercises.name: Calm Greetings
exercises.goal: No jumping on people.
exercises.steps: If he jumps, turn away and ignore until all four paws are on the floor, then crouch and reward calmly.
exercises.rewardTiming: Reward only once all 4 paws are down.
exercises.mistake: Petting or talking to him while he's jumping.

weeks.title: Wait at Doors, Settle on Mat, Place 3Ds, Sound Desensitization

exercises.name: Wait at Doorways
exercises.goal: Doesn't bolt through open doors.
exercises.steps: Before opening any door, ask for a sit. Open slightly; if he surges, close immediately. Reward calm waiting, release with "okay."
exercises.rewardTiming: Reward the calm wait, right before release.
exercises.mistake: Letting him through the door while he's surging forward.

exercises.name: Settle on a Mat
exercises.goal: Relaxes near you during downtime.
exercises.steps: Reward calm lying-down behavior near you at random intervals (e.g., dinner, TV), gradually stretching time between rewards.
exercises.rewardTiming: Random intervals during calm behavior.
exercises.mistake: Only rewarding right when he lies down, never for staying calm afterward.

exercises.name: Place — Distance, Duration, Distraction
exercises.goal: Holds place with 3D challenges, reward-only.
exercises.steps: Distance: step back before returning to reward, increase gradually. Duration: stretch calm time with intermittent rewards. Distraction: add mild distractions (dropped toy, person walking by); reset calmly with a lure if he breaks.
exercises.rewardTiming: Intermittent throughout, mark on successful hold.
exercises.mistake: Adding two of the 3 D's (distance/duration/distraction) at once.

exercises.name: Sound & Sensory Desensitization
exercises.goal: Neutral response to household/outdoor sounds.
exercises.steps: Play recordings (vacuum, doorbell, traffic) at low volume while feeding treats; increase volume gradually over days.
exercises.rewardTiming: Treat continuously while sound plays, stop when sound stops.
exercises.mistake: Jumping straight to full volume.

weeks.title: Outdoor Recall, Impulse Control Games, Guest Greeting Rehearsal

exercises.name: Outdoor Recall (Fenced Yard Only)
exercises.goal: Reliable recall outdoors on a long line.
exercises.steps: Use a long line (per ground-quarantine rules — no public parks yet). Call "Simba, come!" and reward heavily every time, even if slow.
exercises.rewardTiming: Heavy reward on every arrival, no matter the delay.
exercises.mistake: Punishing a slow or reluctant recall.

exercises.name: "It's Your Choice" Impulse Control Game
exercises.goal: Self-control around tempting objects.
exercises.steps: Hold treats in an open palm. If he lunges, close your fist. The instant he backs off/sits, open your palm and let him take a treat.
exercises.rewardTiming: Only after he disengages from lunging.
exercises.mistake: Opening your hand while he's still pushing at it.

exercises.name: Rehearsed Guest Greetings
exercises.goal: Calm settle behavior when people arrive.
exercises.steps: Have a household member walk out and back in repeatedly while Simba practices settling on his mat; reward calm behavior each time.
exercises.rewardTiming: Reward calm settle during the simulated arrival.
exercises.mistake: Doing this only once instead of several repetitions.

weeks.title: Generalizing Commands, Carried Public Exposure, Longer Settle

exercises.name: Generalize All Commands
exercises.goal: Commands work in new rooms/locations.
exercises.steps: Practice sit, down, come, and place in the backyard, garage, and (carried) on walks.
exercises.rewardTiming: Same as original command training — mark and reward on correct response.
exercises.mistake: Assuming a command learned in the kitchen automatically transfers elsewhere.

exercises.name: Carried Public Exposure Sessions
exercises.goal: Comfortable with new sights/sounds/people while carried.
exercises.steps: Carry Simba to a pet-friendly store, busy sidewalk, or park bench (per ground-quarantine protocol), pairing new stimuli with treats and calm praise.
exercises.rewardTiming: Continuous light treating paired with novel stimuli.
exercises.mistake: Putting him down on public ground before vaccination is complete.

exercises.name: Extended Settle
exercises.goal: Settles for 10–15 minutes in a new location.
exercises.steps: Bring his mat to a low-distraction public setting (car, porch) and practice settle there for 10–15 minutes.
exercises.rewardTiming: Intermittent reward for sustained calm.
exercises.mistake: Choosing a high-distraction location too soon.

exercises.name: Command Fluency Check
exercises.goal: First-cue response, no lure, in 3+ rooms.
exercises.steps: Test sit, down, come, stay (10s+), place (1min+), leave it, wait at door, settle — in at least 3 different rooms.
exercises.rewardTiming: Reward each correct first-try response.
exercises.mistake: Testing in only one familiar room and assuming fluency.

exercises.name: Confidence-Building on Novel Surfaces
exercises.goal: Comfortable getting on/off new stable objects.
exercises.steps: Practice stepping on/off a step stool or sturdy box using the same reward-only shaping as the Place command.
exercises.rewardTiming: Mark and reward each successful step-on/off.
exercises.mistake: Using unstable or wobbly objects that could scare him.

exercises.name: Full Curriculum Review
exercises.goal: All Week 1–7 skills solid and generalized.
exercises.steps: Re-run the fluency check from Week 7 across all locations used so far; note any skill scoring below 80% success.
exercises.rewardTiming: Reward all correct responses; extra repetition on weak skills.
exercises.mistake: Moving to advanced training before core skills are consistent.

exercises.name: Next-Stage Readiness Review
exercises.goal: Decide if/when to add leash-pressure or tool-based training.
exercises.steps: Confirm full 16-week vaccination booster completion with your vet before lifting ground-quarantine. Only then consider structured leash/heel work (e.g., Master the Walk course). Reactive to Neutral / E-Collar courses only if a specific issue emerges later — not by default.
exercises.rewardTiming: N/A — planning checkpoint.
exercises.mistake: Introducing leash-pressure corrections or e-collar tools before physical/behavioral readiness.
